questions.question: The Berlin Wall went up overnight in August 1961. Why did East Germany build it?
options: West Germany had openly threatened to annex East Berlin
Soviet troops needed a defensible line to hold against NATO
Skilled workers were leaving west at an unsustainable rate
It replaced an older wall destroyed during the fighting
questions.answer: Skilled workers were leaving west at an unsustainable rate
questions.explanation: Around 3.5 million East Germans, roughly a fifth of the population, had left since 1949, disproportionately doctors, engineers and the young. Berlin was the last open crossing. Construction began overnight on 13 August with barbed wire, cutting streets, tram lines and families mid-sentence. The official name was the Anti-Fascist Protection Rampart, though it was plainly built to keep people in. At least 140 died attempting to cross.
questions.memory_hook: About 3.5 million had already left, a fifth of the population and heavily weighted to doctors, engineers and the young. Berlin was the last hole. They strung wire overnight on 13 August, cutting streets and families in half. Officially it was an anti-fascist rampart; it faced inward.

questions.question: Diamond scores 10 on the Mohs hardness scale. What does that scale actually measure?
options: Density relative to an equal volume of water
What scratches what, not how much force it survives
Resistance to shattering under a hammer blow
How much heat a mineral tolerates before deforming
questions.answer: What scratches what, not how much force it survives
questions.explanation: Mohs is an ordinal scratch test: each mineral scratches those below it, nothing more. It says nothing about toughness, which is why a diamond can be split with a well-placed hammer strike despite being the hardest natural substance. The scale is also not linear. Diamond at 10 is roughly four times harder than corundum at 9, while the gaps lower down are far smaller.
questions.memory_hook: Mohs just ranks what scratches what. It says nothing about toughness, which is why the hardest natural substance still shatters under a hammer. It is not linear either: the jump from 9 to 10 is about four times, while the low-end gaps are tiny.

questions.question: Brazil has won five World Cups. What happened the one time they hosted before 2014?
options: They lost the deciding match at home to Uruguay
They withdrew before the tournament over funding
They won without conceding a single goal
The tournament was cancelled after a stadium collapse
questions.answer: They lost the deciding match at home to Uruguay
questions.explanation: The 1950 final round ended with Brazil needing only a draw against Uruguay in front of around 200,000 at the Maracana. They lost 2-1. It is called the Maracanazo, and Brazil changed its kit afterward because the white shirts were considered unlucky, adopting the yellow now universally recognised. Goalkeeper Moacir Barbosa was blamed for decades and said late in life that the maximum sentence in Brazil is thirty years and he had served fifty.
questions.memory_hook: 1950, at home, needing only a draw against Uruguay in front of 200,000 at the Maracana, and they lost 2-1. The Maracanazo. They ditched the white kit as unlucky and adopted the yellow. Barbosa, the keeper, said Brazil's maximum sentence is thirty years and he had served fifty.

questions.question: Adele names her albums after her age at the time of writing. What broke that pattern?
options: 21 referred to the number of songs she demoed
19 was named for the year it was recorded, not her age
25 was originally titled 24 before a late change
30 came out when she was 33, delayed by her divorce
questions.answer: 30 came out when she was 33, delayed by her divorce
questions.explanation: The numbers mark the age at which the material was written rather than release. 30 was written around her divorce and released when she was 33, and she has described it as an explanation to her son. She also had vocal cord surgery after 21 and could not speak for weeks. 21 has sold over 31 million copies, one of the best-selling albums of the century.
questions.memory_hook: The number is her age when she wrote it, not when it came out. 30 was written around her divorce and released at 33, framed partly as an explanation for her son. She had vocal cord surgery after 21 and could not speak for weeks. 21 has sold over 31 million.

questions.question: Victoria Falls is neither the tallest nor the widest waterfall. What record does it hold?
options: The only waterfall visible from low Earth orbit
The greatest volume discharged in a single second
The largest single sheet of falling water anywhere
The oldest waterfall still flowing on any continent
questions.answer: The largest single sheet of falling water anywhere
questions.explanation: At around 1,700m wide and 108m high it forms the biggest continuous curtain of water on Earth, though Angel Falls is far taller and Khone Falls far wider. The river drops into a narrow zigzag gorge system carved as the falls retreated upstream along cracks in the basalt over hundreds of thousands of years. Each gorge marks a former position of the falls, so you can read its history backwards along the canyon.
questions.memory_hook: About 1,700m wide and 108m high, the largest unbroken curtain of falling water anywhere, though Angel Falls is taller and Khone wider. It drops into a zigzag gorge that marks where the falls used to be, retreating upstream along cracks in the basalt over hundreds of thousands of years.

questions.question: The Meiji Restoration stripped the samurai of their status. What was the Satsuma Rebellion?
options: A naval mutiny by officers loyal to the deposed shogun
A merchant strike that shut down Osaka for several months
A tax uprising by farmers against the new imperial government
A samurai revolt in 1877, crushed by peasant conscripts
questions.answer: A samurai revolt in 1877, crushed by peasant conscripts
questions.explanation: Saigo Takamori, himself a leading figure in the Restoration, led disaffected Satsuma samurai against the government he had helped create. They were defeated by a conscript army of commoners with modern rifles and artillery, which settled the argument about whether hereditary warrior status still meant anything militarily. Saigo died at Shiroyama. He was posthumously pardoned in 1889 and is still a widely admired figure in Japan.
questions.memory_hook: Saigo Takamori, who had helped create the new government, led disaffected samurai against it in 1877 and was destroyed by conscripted commoners with rifles and artillery. That ended any argument about hereditary warriors mattering militarily. He was pardoned posthumously and is still admired.

questions.question: Rowling wrote much of the first Harry Potter book in Edinburgh cafes. Why there?
options: Walking her baby to sleep, then writing while she napped
A publisher required her to write on the premises
Her flat had no electricity for most of that winter
She was banned from the university library nearby
questions.answer: Walking her baby to sleep, then writing while she napped
questions.explanation: Rowling was a single mother on state benefits, and walking her daughter until she fell asleep then writing in a warm cafe was cheaper than heating a flat. Twelve publishers rejected the manuscript. Bloomsbury accepted after the chairman's eight-year-old daughter read the first chapter and demanded the rest, and advised Rowling to get a day job since children's books do not pay. The initial print run was 500 copies.
questions.memory_hook: Single mother on benefits, walking her daughter to sleep then writing in a warm cafe because it was cheaper than heating the flat. Twelve publishers said no. Bloomsbury said yes because the chairman's eight-year-old demanded the rest, then told her to keep a day job. First print run: 500 copies.

questions.question: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. How is that number arrived at?
options: By counting the oldest known stars and adding a safety margin
From the cosmic microwave background's temperature ripples
By measuring how far the most distant galaxy has travelled
From the decay rate of uranium found in the oldest meteorites
questions.answer: From the cosmic microwave background's temperature ripples
questions.explanation: The Planck satellite mapped microscopic temperature variations in the afterglow of the Big Bang and fitted them to a cosmological model, yielding 13.787 billion years with roughly 0.2% uncertainty. Independent checks from the oldest known stars and from the abundance of light elements agree. There is an open problem though: measuring the expansion rate using nearby supernovae gives a different answer than the microwave background does, a discrepancy called the Hubble tension.
questions.memory_hook: Planck mapped tiny temperature ripples in the Big Bang's afterglow and fitted them to a model: 13.787 billion years, give or take 0.2%. The oldest stars agree. But measuring expansion using nearby supernovae gives a different number, and nobody has resolved that yet. It is called the Hubble tension.

questions.question: San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic. What is its founding story?
options: A stonemason fled Roman persecution and hid on a mountain
It was left unclaimed when the Papal States were divided
Napoleon granted it sovereignty as a diplomatic gesture
Venetian merchants bought independence in the 1300s
questions.answer: A stonemason fled Roman persecution and hid on a mountain
questions.explanation: Tradition dates it to 301 AD, when Marinus, a Christian stonemason, took refuge on Monte Titano. It has stayed independent largely by being too small and too awkwardly placed to bother conquering. Napoleon offered to expand its territory and San Marino declined, reasoning that staying tiny was the survival strategy. It sheltered around 100,000 refugees during the Second World War, roughly ten times its own population.
questions.memory_hook: A Christian stonemason named Marinus hid on Monte Titano in 301 AD, and it has survived by being too small and awkward to be worth taking. Napoleon offered it more land and it refused, on the grounds that staying tiny was the whole strategy. It sheltered 100,000 refugees in WWII, ten times its population.

questions.question: The Trail of Tears removed the Cherokee in 1838. What made it legally extraordinary?
options: Congress voted against it and was overruled by the states
It was carried out under a treaty no Cherokee had signed
The Supreme Court had already ruled the removal unlawful
The Cherokee were US citizens with full voting rights
questions.answer: The Supreme Court had already ruled the removal unlawful
questions.explanation: In Worcester v. Georgia (1832) Chief Justice Marshall held the Cherokee Nation sovereign and Georgia's laws inapplicable to it. Jackson declined to enforce the ruling. Removal proceeded under the Treaty of New Echota, signed by a faction of around 100 Cherokee with no authority to represent the nation, and rejected by a petition carrying over 15,000 Cherokee signatures. Roughly 4,000 of 16,000 died on the march.
questions.memory_hook: The Supreme Court had already ruled in 1832 that the Cherokee were sovereign and Georgia had no authority. Jackson simply did not enforce it. Removal went ahead under a treaty signed by about 100 people with no authority, against a petition with 15,000 signatures. Around 4,000 of 16,000 died.

questions.question: Pulp Fiction (1994) tells its story out of order. What does that structure accomplish?
options: It conceals the identity of the narrator until the end
A character killed midway is alive again in the final scene
Each viewing reveals a different chronological sequence
The film can be watched starting from any chapter
questions.answer: A character killed midway is alive again in the final scene
questions.explanation: Vincent Vega is shot dead partway through and appears alive in the closing diner scene, because that scene occurs earlier chronologically. Tarantino has said the structure lets a film end on a character's redemption rather than his death. It cost around $8 million, made over $200 million, won the Palme d'Or, and revived John Travolta's career from near-total obscurity.
questions.memory_hook: Vincent Vega is shot dead midway and is alive in the last scene, because that scene happens earlier in time. Tarantino wanted to end on redemption rather than a corpse. Made for $8 million, took over $200 million, won the Palme d'Or, and pulled Travolta out of obscurity.

questions.question: An ace in tennis is a serve the returner never touches. What is the fastest ever recorded?
options: Around 210 km/h, unchanged since the wooden era
Around 180 km/h, the physical limit of a human arm
Around 263 km/h, by Australian Sam Groth in 2012
Around 320 km/h, set with an oversized racquet
questions.answer: Around 263 km/h, by Australian Sam Groth in 2012
questions.explanation: Groth hit 263.4 km/h at a Challenger event in Busan, though the ATP does not formally ratify it because the radar was not their standard equipment. Their recognised record is John Isner's 253 km/h. Serving speed rose sharply once graphite replaced wood in the 1980s. Isner also played the longest match in history at Wimbledon in 2010, 11 hours 5 minutes across three days, with a final set of 70-68.
questions.memory_hook: Sam Groth hit 263.4 km/h in 2012, though the ATP does not ratify it because the radar was not theirs. Their official record is Isner's 253. Speeds jumped when graphite replaced wood in the 1980s. Isner also played an 11-hour Wimbledon match with a 70-68 final set.
